sun.upright:
The man in this card is tiptoeing, and Aries doesn't tiptoe. An Aries Sun wants to be first through the door and wants everyone to know it was them, so a card about the quiet solo move sits a bit oddly on you. The astrology is kinder than that sounds. The card is the Moon in the last ten degrees of Aquarius, and Aquarius is sextile Aries, two signs apart, an easy opening that you still have to take on purpose. Air and fire get on, too. Aquarian air gives Aries fire something to burn with, so a bit of strategy can make the drive go further.

You'll know the feeling of having worked out a cleverer way round a problem and being desperate to announce it before it's done. Aries wants the credit and the Seven wants cover. The Moon is only a guest in Aries, coloured by Mars, your ruler, so whatever you're keeping quiet you're keeping quiet impatiently, and the silence tends to break early. I've seen a lot of Aries Suns win the argument by force and lose the thing they actually wanted, when a side route would have got them there with no fuss at all.

At work this is the colleague or manager you can't beat head-on, and for once going round them is the smart move. With a sibling or an old rival it's the fight you keep having in exactly the same place. With money it might be a side project you're building before you tell anyone. Pick the one situation where charging in hasn't worked and try the quiet route for a fortnight. Just make sure it's a route you'd be happy to explain afterwards.
sun.reversed:
Upside down, the Seven on an Aries Sun often means you gave the plan away before it had a chance. You told the room, you let the rival see it coming, or you got bored of the quiet part and went in swinging. The other version is sneakier and much less like you. A Mars-coloured Moon, turned sideways, becomes point-scoring behind someone's back, the dig in the group chat you'd never make to their face.

At work that's the email copied to the boss to make a point. At home it's winning a fight by bringing up something from two years ago. Either way an Aries Sun ends up feeling slightly grubby, because you're an upfront sign and this isn't upfront. If there's someone you've been sniping at, say the thing to them directly, once, and then let it go.

moon.upright:
A Moon card landing on your Moon doubles the focus, and with an Aries Moon it lands on feelings that fire first and ask questions later. You need to act on what you feel. Sitting with something makes you twitchy. The Seven of Swords asks for the opposite, a feeling kept back while you work out what to do with it. The Moon has no particular standing in Aries and takes on Mars's temper, so your emotions come in hot. But Aquarius is two signs from Aries, a sextile, and air feeds fire, which gives you a real chance to add a bit of cool strategy to all that heat.

From the inside it feels like holding your tongue and being surprised you managed it. Something's annoyed you, a comment, a slight, a plan changed without anyone asking you, and instead of reacting on the spot you've gone quiet and started thinking. For an Aries Moon that's unfamiliar and it can feel like sulking. It isn't quite. It's closer to keeping your powder dry, and it suits you better than you'd expect, as long as it doesn't turn into a secret campaign.

With a partner it's the row you didn't start, and the calmer conversation two days later. With a parent it might be deciding not to rise to the old bait at a family lunch. In the body you'll notice where the unspent heat goes, the jaw, the shoulders, a restless night. Burn some of it off before you decide what to say. A run, a hard swim, an hour in the garden with a spade.
moon.reversed:
For an Aries Moon, this card reversed often looks like leaving. Not the dramatic exit. The quiet one, where you're hurt, you don't say so, and you slip off early from the party or go cold on a friend without explaining. The Moon in a Mars sign wants to fight. Reversed, it's stopped fighting and started avoiding, and the anger doesn't go anywhere, it just goes underground.

You'll see it in the snappy reply to a question that had nothing to do with it, and in the nights spent rehearsing a showdown you won't have. A partner may feel punished without knowing what for. Pick the person you've gone cold on and tell them, in two sentences, what they did. It'll feel far too blunt to you. They'll probably be relieved to know.

rising.upright:
Aries rising usually arrives like a door opened a bit too hard. People meet someone quick, frank and easy to read, and mostly that's accurate. With the Seven of Swords as your mask card, there's a sly edge on that entrance. You're walking in with something up your sleeve, a plan, an angle, a reason for being there you haven't mentioned, and the Moon in a Mars-ruled sign gives it a competitive flavour. The sextile between Aquarius and Aries helps. Fire and air get on, so the strategy doesn't slow you down much. It just gives the charge a direction.

Where it pulls is that Aries rising has never been much good at poker. Your face shows things. So there's an odd strain in being the one holding the hidden card, because you can feel it on your face and you suspect others can see it too. Sometimes they can. Strangers may read you as up to something, and they're right, even if what you're up to is perfectly decent, like wanting the job more badly than you're letting on.

In a job interview it's playing it cooler than you feel and asking the question that shows you've done your homework. In a negotiation, over a car or a rent increase, it's keeping your top number to yourself, which for Aries is genuinely hard. With a new group it's watching for a while before you take over. Go into the next first meeting with one thing you've decided not to say, and see what you learn by holding it back.
rising.reversed:
With this card reversed, Aries rising tends to get caught with the swords still in its arms. The plan was clever, and your face gave it away in the first five minutes, or you got impatient and said the quiet part out loud. It can go the other way too. You're so busy trying to look like you've got an angle that people find you cagey, which is an odd look on a sign that's usually so open.

At work it's the push for a promotion that everyone saw coming because you couldn't help mentioning it. In a new relationship it's playing a game about who texts first and getting bored of your own game. The fix suits Aries rising, which is to drop the tactics and say what you want at the start. Say it in the first conversation and see what comes back.

sun.upright:
Taurus Suns like the long way round, the proper way, the method that's been tested and won't let them down. So a card about a clever shortcut isn't an obvious fit, and the astrology says as much. Aquarius and Taurus are square, both fixed signs, three apart, and when two fixed signs meet neither moves easily. There's air against earth as well, the idea against the proof. And yet the card's planet is the Moon, and Taurus is where the Moon is exalted, the sign that honours it most. So underneath the friction the card has something to offer you, an instinct you can trust about what's worth protecting.

From the inside this feels like being asked to cut a corner and hating it. You've built something steadily, a skill, a savings account, a reputation for being reliable, and the Seven says there's a faster, less obvious way to the next stage. Part of you is tempted. Most of you is suspicious. That suspicion is partly good sense and partly the Taurus habit of treating anything unfamiliar as a trick, and with fixed against fixed you can dig in over the question for weeks.

With money it might be a smarter arrangement you've been ignoring, the account you haven't switched, the pay conversation you didn't start because it felt pushy. At work it's the job you still do by hand because you always have. The Moon also rules the middle decan of Taurus, the Six of Pentacles, the card of giving and receiving fairly, and that's a good test to apply. Try the quicker route somewhere nobody loses anything by it.
sun.reversed:
On a Taurus Sun, the reversed card tends to be about something you're holding on to that isn't quite yours to hold. Money, credit for work, or a position you're keeping by quietly making sure nobody else learns how to do it. The Moon is at its strongest in Taurus, and a strong Moon hangs on. Upside down, the hanging on turns a little sly.

At work it's the knowledge you never write down, so you stay the only one who knows. At home it can be the purchase you haven't mentioned, or savings a partner doesn't know about, kept for reasons that felt sensible at the time. None of it is dramatic, which is why it can run for years. Pick one of those things and bring it into the open with the person it affects, before they come across it on their own.

moon.upright:
Exalted in Taurus, the Moon is about as content as it ever gets, and a Taurus Moon is the Moon doing what it does best, settling, feeding, holding on to what feels safe. A Moon card drawn on your Moon picks that up directly. What the Seven of Swords adds is a private streak. You're looking after yourself in ways nobody else sees, and some of it you'd rather they didn't.

Aquarius squares Taurus, and air sits awkwardly on earth, so the comfort you're after and this card's cool, detached mood grind against each other. It can feel like managing your needs in secret, the chocolate in the glovebox, the afternoon off you haven't told anyone about, the worry you're keeping to yourself so the household stays calm. Some of that is fine, even healthy. The trouble with a square between two fixed signs is that a private habit can set hard. What began as a bit of self-care you kept quiet becomes the thing you can't mention.

With a partner, it shows as being the calm one while privately stewing over money or a change at home. With the body it's comfort eating, or its opposite, quietly cutting back and saying nothing. Sleep is usually a good gauge, and so is how often you're choosing to be alone to feel better. If there's one thing you've been soothing yourself about in secret, tell someone you trust what it is. The need itself is perfectly reasonable, and it's easier to meet once somebody knows.
moon.reversed:
Reversed, this card can make a Taurus Moon feel robbed, sometimes of something real and sometimes of something imagined. A colleague took the credit, a sibling got more help from a parent, a friend borrowed and never gave it back. The exalted Moon in Taurus holds on hard, and when it thinks something's been taken it goes still and stubborn and keeps a very long record.

At home this looks like a grudge nobody else knows is running. In the body it tends to be tension held low down, the stomach, the throat, the jaw set at night. You might be right about what happened. Even so, a Taurus Moon can sit on it for a year and call that patience. Say to the person what you believe they took, and ask for it back, whether that's the money, the apology or the credit.

rising.upright:
Nobody expects the Taurus rising person to be the one with the plan. You come across as steady, pleasant, a bit slow to commit, somebody who'll be the same next week as today. With this card showing as your mask, the calm front has something going on behind it. The card's Moon is exalted in your rising sign, so it sits comfortably on you, and people will find you easy to trust when they first meet you.

That's the part to be careful with. Aquarius squares Taurus, two fixed signs, so there's a stubborn quality to whatever you're quietly planning. You're patient. You'll let the other person talk, you'll agree pleasantly, and then you'll do what you'd already decided to do. Air and earth disagree about what counts as real, so while you're saying the easy thing you're keeping your own tally of what's actually happening. It works. It can also leave people feeling slightly handled when they work it out later.

In a salary talk or haggling at a market it's the quiet advantage of not seeming to want it much. In a new friendship it's being liked quickly while keeping most of yourself back. At a new job it's being underestimated in the first week and using it. Let one person see the plan early, somebody whose trust you actually want, so the steadiness they see and the thinking behind it match up.
rising.reversed:
When the card's upside down, Taurus rising can come across as immovable in a slightly shifty way. People sense you've made up your mind and aren't saying so. You nod through the meeting and then don't do what was agreed, or you accept plans you've no intention of keeping, because refusing someone to their face feels like too much fuss.

It shows at work as the passive resistance a manager eventually notices, the task that never quite gets started. With friends it's the 'maybe' that everyone knows means no. On a date it can be pleasant company and no information at all. Taurus rising is at its best when it's openly stubborn. So the next time you're going to say no, say it at the time, plainly, and skip the quiet workaround.

sun.upright:
Of all the signs, Gemini is the one this card feels most at home with. Aquarius and Gemini are trine, both air, and a trine between signs of the same element means the card speaks your language without an accent. The Moon has no rank in Gemini and takes its colour from Mercury, your ruler, the planet of wit, messages and the quick change of plan. So the card's cleverness goes straight into your talking. You can find the angle, sell the angle, and have a second one ready by lunchtime.

The same element amplifies, for better and for too much, and ease is the risk. When you're this good at the workaround you stop noticing when you're using it. A Gemini Sun under this card can end up with slightly different stories for different people, not lies exactly, just versions, each tailored to whoever's listening. It feels like being adaptable. After a few weeks it starts to feel like keeping track, and that's the moment to pay attention.

At work this shows up as juggling three projects and quietly letting the one you like least slide, hoping nobody checks. With a brother or sister it's the old habit of talking your way out of trouble. In a friendship group it can be passing on news that wasn't quite yours to pass on. For a while, try telling the same version of things to everyone. You'll find out very quickly where that's hard.
sun.reversed:
Cleverness that's got itself tangled is what this card reversed usually means for a Gemini Sun. Too many versions of the story in circulation, too many half-promises, too many tabs open. A Mercury-coloured Moon loves a plan with moving parts, and upside down it has more parts than you can keep hold of, so something drops. Or you think so many moves ahead that you never make the first one.

At work it's the excuse that needs another excuse to hold it up. Socially it's being caught in a small fib, harmless in itself, that makes someone wonder what else was trimmed. Gemini can talk its way out of that, and probably will. The better move is to simplify. Close a few of the loops, cancel what you can't do, and give people the plain version even when it's less interesting.

moon.upright:
A Gemini Moon settles by talking. You work out what you feel by saying it, texting it, turning it over with three different friends until it makes sense. The Moon takes Mercury's colour in Gemini, and this card is air too, so the pairing runs fast and easy. Aquarius trines Gemini. Same element, no friction. The card doesn't push against you. It pushes you further in the direction you already lean.

Which in this case is toward being clever about feelings. There's a way a Gemini Moon can talk around the thing that actually hurt, making it funny, making it a story, moving to the next subject before anyone, you included, lands on it. The card shows someone slipping off with the swords and a half-smile, and for you the swords are words. You'll recognise the evening where you told a friend all about your week and somehow never mentioned the one conversation that's been bothering you.

In a relationship it's being great company and hard to pin down about what you need. With friends it's being everyone's confidant and nobody's worry. The mind usually shows it at night, when the chatter won't switch off and sleep takes an hour to arrive. Write down, somewhere private, the one thing you keep not mentioning. Just a sentence, and then leave it alone.
moon.reversed:
When this card is reversed for a Gemini Moon, the mind runs the feelings instead of hearing them. You're anxious and you can list eight reasons. You're sad and you've found a funny way to say so. Air on air amplifies, and reversed that goes into overthinking, reading a message five times, drafting replies you don't send, deciding what someone meant from their punctuation. None of it settles anything.

Sleep is where it shows most. So does your phone, which is in your hand a lot. With a partner or a close friend it can come out as a coolness that's really tiredness with your own thoughts. Put the phone in another room for an evening. Then ring one person and say, without the jokes, what's actually on your mind.

rising.upright:
Within ten minutes of meeting someone, Gemini rising has usually found common ground, a joke, a shared bit of gossip, a question that gets them talking. As your mask card the Seven of Swords sharpens that. Aquarius trines Gemini, air to air, and the card's Moon borrows Mercury's colour here, so you're reading rooms quickly and adjusting before anybody notices you've adjusted.

It's a real talent and it has a slippery side. You can be a slightly different person with everyone, not in a calculated way. You pick up what each person responds to and give them that. Strangers leave charmed. People who meet you in two different settings sometimes feel they've met two people. The figure on the card, glancing back over his shoulder, is a fair picture of how this feels from inside, checking how you're being received while you're already moving on to the next conversation.

At a party or a networking do it's working the room brilliantly and leaving without one real conversation. In sales, or any job where you pitch, it's knowing exactly which line will work on which person. On a first date it's keeping things light for so long that the other person wonders if there's anything underneath. Next time you meet someone new, ask one question you'd genuinely like answered and stay on that subject longer than feels natural.
rising.reversed:
Gemini rising with this card reversed can come across as too quick to be trusted. The cleverness shows. People notice the change of subject, the answer that dodges, the story that's grown since last time, and they start keeping a little distance without telling you why. Or you notice them noticing and go stiff, which for a Gemini Ascendant is an unusual and uncomfortable feeling.

At work it's the new colleague who's decided you're a bit slippery on very little evidence. Online it's the comment you wrote to be witty that read as sly. With a new friend it's cancelling twice with a clever excuse. The remedy is boring and it works. Say fewer things, and make each of them something you'd repeat word for word to anyone who asked.

sun.upright:
Cancer's symbol, the crab, has never walked straight at anything, so a card about the sideways approach is less foreign to you than it looks. The Moon rules Cancer, which makes the card's planet the landlord of your Sun sign, and it speaks with some authority. What a Cancer Sun is building is a safe place for its people. What the Seven of Swords says is that you might need to get there by a quieter route than usual, doing something on your own and not explaining it yet.

The difficulty is Aquarius. It sits five signs from Cancer, a quincunx, two signs with nothing in common that have to keep making small adjustments. Air and water don't clash. They've just never been introduced. So the card's cool, private strategy feels unnatural, even though its planet is your ruler. You'd rather protect people in the open, and keeping a plan to yourself, especially from family, can feel like a betrayal even when it's for them. The Moon also rules the last ten degrees of Cancer, the decan of the Four of Cups, so going quiet and pulling back is something your sign already knows how to do. This card just adds a plan.

At home it might be sorting out a problem, a debt, a parent's care, a child's school, before anyone else knows it exists. At work it's the job application you're keeping quiet until you hear back. With your mother, or whoever mothered you, it could be doing something your own way without asking first. Look at the plan you're keeping private and ask who it's protecting. If the answer is them, carry on.
sun.reversed:
For a Cancer Sun the reversed card often shows up as protecting people by keeping things from them. The letter from the bank you haven't mentioned, the problem at work, the thing a relative said that you decided nobody else needed to hear. The Moon rules your sign, so the instinct to shield is strong and it feels like love. Upside down, the shielding turns into managing, and the people you're protecting start to sense there's a room they aren't allowed into.

At home it becomes a tension nobody can name. At work it's quietly carrying a load you never told anyone about. Resentment builds in both places. Pick one thing you've been sparing the people you love and let them have it, gently. They're usually tougher than a Cancer Sun gives them credit for.

moon.upright:
This is the Moon three times over. A Moon card, read on your Moon, which sits in Cancer, the one sign the Moon rules. So whatever the Seven of Swords has to say, it's saying it loudly to the part of you that needs to feel safe and needed and at home. That much Moon brings the card's quietest meaning forward, the private motive. There's something you want for yourself that you haven't said.

What complicates it is that the card's sign, Aquarius, is quincunx Cancer. Five signs apart, no shared language. Aquarius is happy to step back from the group and do its own thing, and a Cancer Moon feels that as a kind of disloyalty. So wanting something for yourself, a weekend alone, a different job, fewer Sundays at your parents', gets slipped in sideways, taken quietly and with some guilt, a bit like the man on the card creeping off with the swords. You look after everyone. Taking a share for yourself without asking feels like stealing, even when it's only fair.

In a family this is the Sunday you didn't go over and didn't explain. With a partner it's the need you meet on your own because asking feels too exposed. The body tends to hold it in the stomach, and you might notice you're eating for comfort, or hardly at all. Say the need out loud to one person, as plainly as you can. 'I want a day to myself' is allowed.
moon.reversed:
With the card reversed, a Cancer Moon can go into full retreat. The Moon is strong in its own sign, and upside down that strength goes into hiding, the shell pulled over, the hurt kept private, the long silence you're hoping someone will notice. It can also turn into keeping score of every small neglect while telling everyone you're fine.

At home this is being very helpful and slightly cold at the same time. With old friends it's the invitation you turned down because they didn't ask the way you wanted to be asked. Sleep gets shallow and the past gets loud, family memories turning up at odd hours. Ring the person you've been quietly waiting on. You don't need to make a case. Tell them you've missed them and let them take it from there.

rising.upright:
With Cancer rising, the Moon is your chart ruler, the planet that owns your Ascendant, so a Moon card turning up as your mask speaks straight to how you come across. This one says you're coming across as more private than usual. Cancer rising already meets people with a bit of shell up, kind and attentive but careful, and the Seven of Swords puts a plan behind the shell. You're watching, working out who's safe, deciding what to share, and you haven't let anyone see the working.

The card's sign, Aquarius, is quincunx Cancer, and the two keep having to adjust to each other. Aquarius is cool and fine being a bit apart. Cancer rising wants to belong and won't go first. So you might end up playing it cooler than you feel and then being hurt that people took you at your word. Strangers can usually read a Cancer Ascendant's moods, and with this card what they read is reserve, maybe even a sense that you're hiding something. Mostly you're protecting yourself until you know the room.

In a new workplace it's being liked and not quite known for the first few months. At the school gate or a new club it's the slow circle of people you let in. On a first date it's asking all the questions so you never have to answer any. Next time somebody asks you something personal, answer it properly. Give them one real detail and let them see it.
rising.reversed:
Cancer rising with the Seven reversed can slip out of things before they've started. You see a possible hurt coming and you're gone, the early exit from the party, the job you didn't apply for, the date cancelled with a vague excuse. The Moon rules your Ascendant, and upside down it protects you so thoroughly that nobody can reach you, including the people you'd quite like to let in.

In a new team it gets you thought of as aloof when really you're shy. With friends it's the pattern of vanishing for a few weeks and coming back as if nothing happened, which they've learnt to live with and don't love. Pick one thing you'd normally slip out of, a dinner, a class, a phone call, and stay for the whole of it.

sun.upright:
Two swords left standing in the ground and a man creeping off, hoping nobody turns round. For a Leo Sun that's an awkward picture, because you don't creep off from anything. You want to be seen doing what you do and you want your name on it. The card's sign is Aquarius, which sits directly opposite Leo, so this is the far end of your own axis looking back at you. Leo stands in the middle of the room. Aquarius stands at the edge of it, watching the group and quietly deciding to go its own way.

An opposition pulls toward balance, and in practice that feels like being asked to do something clever without taking the bow. The Moon is only a visitor in Leo and borrows its colour from the Sun, your ruler, so the card's private motive is still about your pride and your plans. It just wants them kept in your pocket for a while. Air feeds fire, so the strategy won't dampen you. You'll feel the itch to tell someone how smart the move was, though, and I've seen plenty of Leo Suns sink a good plan by announcing it at dinner.

At work this is the project you're steering from behind someone else's name, which might be the right call for once. With something creative, a book, a band, a business idea, it's working on it privately until it's good enough to show. In a friendship group it can mean stepping back from being the organiser to see who steps forward. Keep one plan to yourself until it's finished.
sun.reversed:
With the card reversed, a Leo Sun's pride and the card's slyness can get tangled together. You took a shortcut and now you can't admit it, because admitting it means looking less than magnificent. Or someone else took the credit for your work and you're too proud to say so, so you sulk in public and call it dignity. The Sun-coloured Moon wants to be admired even for its secrets, which is a hard thing to pull off.

At work it's the small exaggeration on the CV or in the meeting that you now have to keep living up to. With a partner it's refusing to say you were hurt because it would mean admitting you cared. Pick the one story about yourself that's been slightly polished and tell someone the unpolished version. Leo is warmer and far easier to love when it's been caught out a bit and can laugh about it.

moon.upright:
A Leo Moon needs to feel wanted, warmly and out loud. You're soothed by being noticed, by someone remembering the thing you said last week, by a bit of fuss on your birthday. The Seven of Swords is a Moon card with an Aquarian streak, and Aquarius is Leo's opposite sign, so the card arrives from the one place in the zodiac that can happily go without applause. That's the pull you'll feel. Part of you wants the reassurance and part of you has decided to stop asking for it.

The Moon is a guest in Leo, coloured by the Sun, so even your private moods have a touch of theatre about them. What the opposition does is turn the need inside out. Instead of saying 'I felt left out', you go cool, you make a clever joke about it, you arrange to be busy the next time they ask. It's a pride-saving manoeuvre and you'll know the feeling, the little glow of not needing anyone that fades by about ten o'clock at night. Air and fire get along, so the distance can be useful for a while. It helps you see a situation straight without drowning in hurt feelings.

With a partner it's the evening you acted fine when you wanted a hug. With friends it's the party you left early so nobody could see you weren't having fun. The chest and the upper back are where Leo Moons often carry this, a tightness that eases once you've been properly held. Ask one person, directly, for the attention you've been pretending not to want.
moon.reversed:
Reversed on a Leo Moon, the card often looks like a performance of being fine. You're hurt and you're throwing a better party than ever, posting more, laughing louder, so that whoever hurt you can see how little it mattered. The Sun-coloured Moon hides its wounds behind a show, and the Aquarian distance gives the show a cool finish that's quite convincing.

It shows up in friendships as the drama you're pretending you're above, and at home as a sulk dressed up as independence. Sleep can go, too, because a Leo Moon replays what was said and what it should have said back. Stop performing for one evening. Tell the person you're closest to what actually stung, in the plainest words you've got, and let them fuss over you.

rising.upright:
Leo rising walks into a room and the room turns, mostly because you expect it to. The Sun rules your Ascendant, and with the Seven of Swords as your mask card there's something going on behind the big, warm entrance. Aquarius, the card's sign, sits exactly opposite Leo, which makes it the sign on your Descendant, the cusp of the seventh house, where you meet other people one to one. So this card is familiar territory. It's the kind of person you tend to be drawn to or tangled up with, the cool one at the edge with their own agenda, and this time you're wearing a bit of that yourself.

It feels like holding back. You're still charming, still the one who fills the silence, but you're watching while you do it. There's a plan behind the performance, a reason you've come to this particular dinner or taken this particular meeting, and you haven't said what it is. The Moon, visiting and coloured by the Sun, keeps the private motive fairly flattering to you. People will sense the warmth first and the calculation second, if they notice it at all.

In a job interview it's the confident front with a very clear idea of what you'll accept and what you won't. On a first date it's being great fun while deciding quite coolly whether they're worth it. At a family gathering it's playing the role everyone expects while working out how to leave early without upsetting anyone. Let one person see the calculation along with the charm, and see how they respond.
rising.reversed:
When the Seven is upside down for Leo rising, the act starts to show its seams. You're working a room and someone clocks that you're working it. Or you've dressed a plan up as spontaneous fun and the people around you have started to feel used as an audience. Leo rising usually gets away with a lot on warmth alone. With this card reversed, warmth isn't quite enough cover.

It turns up at work as the pitch that was all presentation and very little underneath, and in friendships as the suspicion that you only turn up when there's something in it for you, which is unfair but hard to shake once it's started. In love it can be a partner who's tired of the show. Drop the performance somewhere small. Go to something where you aren't the host or the star and have nothing to gain, and just be good company.

sun.upright:
Virgo Suns would like to do things properly, by the method that works, checked twice. A card about cutting a corner lands on that like a spilt drink on a clean desk. Aquarius and Virgo are quincunx, five signs apart, and signs that far apart don't share an element, a mode or much of an outlook, so they have to keep making small adjustments to live with each other. Air and earth are opposed as well, the idea against the proof. The card has a clever plan. You want to see the evidence first.

The Moon is a visitor in Virgo, coloured by Mercury, your ruler, and that's where the two sides can meet, since Mercury is cleverness too. What you'll feel is a quiet argument between your standards and your shrewdness. You can see the shortcut perfectly well. You probably spotted it before anyone. You just don't trust anything that easy, and a lot of the time you're right to be wary. Some of the time you aren't, and the long way round is costing you weekends you won't get back.

At work it's the process you've been following because it's the process, when a smarter version would take half the time. With your health it's the routine you keep up out of duty rather than because it still helps. With a colleague it might be admitting that their lazy-looking method actually works. Choose one task that eats your week and design the quickest honest way to do it.
sun.reversed:
For a Virgo Sun, the reversed Seven tends to mean hiding a mistake. A small one, usually. A missed figure in the spreadsheet, a step skipped in a job you're known for doing thoroughly, a promise that quietly slid. Virgo holds itself to such a high standard that owning up feels worse than the error, so you fix it privately and hope nobody noticed. A Mercury-coloured Moon is good at tidying the evidence.

The strain goes into the body and the evenings, lying awake checking things, rewriting an email four times. At work it can mean doing someone else's job as well as your own so their slip doesn't reflect on the team, and resenting it. Tell the person it affects what went wrong, in one sentence, with the fix attached. You'll be trusted more for it, and you know that already.

moon.upright:
Virgo Moons settle by sorting. When you're upset you clean the kitchen, write a list, fix whatever can be fixed, and the feeling calms down once there's some order around it. The Seven of Swords brings in a cooler, more secretive mood. The card's Moon is only visiting Virgo and takes Mercury's colour, so it thinks about feelings more readily than it has them, and with air opposed to earth the thinking drifts a long way from the body, which is where Virgo usually handles things.

Aquarius is quincunx Virgo. The two don't naturally understand each other, so you'll feel the adjustment. It can look like quietly managing your own anxiety with systems nobody else knows about, checking the lock three times, private rules about bedtime or what counts as a proper dinner, the rehearsed answer for when someone asks how you are. None of it is dramatic. It's a way of coping on your own that keeps everyone else out of it, and the picture of a person slipping off alone with an armful of swords isn't a bad description of how that feels.

With a partner it shows as being very useful and hard to comfort. At work it's the extra hours you don't mention. In the body a Virgo Moon under strain tends to notice the gut first, and sleep that comes late because the mind is still tidying. Tell someone about one of your private rules, one of the small ones that keep you feeling safe. Saying it aloud usually loosens it a bit.
moon.reversed:
Turned over, this card can make a Virgo Moon critical in a sideways way. Instead of saying you're hurt, you find fault. The way someone loaded the dishwasher, the typo in their message, the tone of their voice on the phone. The Mercury-coloured Moon picks at details because the real thing is too uncomfortable to pick at, and the Aquarian coolness makes it all sound perfectly reasonable.

At home that's a partner who feels they can't do anything right and doesn't know why. With your own body it's worrying at small twinges and ignoring plain tiredness. Work may get the best of you and home the leftovers. Next time you catch yourself correcting someone, stop and ask what you're actually upset about. Then say that thing to them instead.

rising.upright:
First impressions of Virgo rising tend to be tidy, alert, helpful, a person who's noticed what needs doing before anyone asked. Mercury rules your Ascendant, and the Moon on this card borrows Mercury's colour in Virgo, so in one sense the Seven of Swords sits on your manner quite naturally. You're observant and quick. People just don't always see how much you're taking in.

The friction comes from the quincunx between Aquarius and Virgo and the clash of air with earth. The card wants to move on its own logic and keep its reasons private. Virgo rising wants to be seen as reliable and above board. So you can find yourself doing something slightly out of character, holding back information in a meeting, letting someone assume you agree, playing a bit dim to see what they'll say, and then feeling oddly exposed about it. The strategy is sound. It just doesn't match your idea of yourself as the straightforward one.

In a new job this is quietly learning where the real influence sits before you commit to anyone. In a negotiation, a lease or a pay rise, it's having done the homework and keeping that quiet until the right moment. On a first date it can mean asking careful questions and giving careful, slightly edited answers. Before the next meeting that matters, decide which one fact you'll keep back and why, so it's a choice you've made on purpose and can live with.
rising.reversed:
Virgo rising with the card upside down can come across as sneaky when it's really just nervous. You over-prepare, you hedge, you give an answer that's technically true and avoids the question, and people pick up on the gap. The quincunx makes that small mismatch between how you mean to come across and how you're read feel much bigger than it is.

It tends to show at work in reviews and interviews, where your caution reads as hiding something. With new friends it's the vagueness about your weekend, your family, your past, which you think of as privacy and they find a bit odd. Answer the next personal question with a real answer, even a short one, like where you grew up or what you did on Sunday.

sun.upright:
Libra Suns are building a life that's fair and graceful and gets along with people, and a card about slipping off with the goods would seem the last thing you'd draw. The astrology says it fits better than that. Aquarius trines Libra, both air, so the card and your sign speak the same language. The Moon rules the first ten degrees of Libra too, through the Two of Swords, the card of the decision put off, so this card's planet already has a foothold in your sign. And here the Moon takes on Venus's colour, which makes its private strategy charming more often than cold.

Same element amplifies, for better and for too much. Libra's diplomacy and the Seven's tact are close cousins, and together they can tip into telling each person the version that keeps them happy. You'll recognise agreeing with both sides of an argument on the same afternoon and half meaning it both times. It isn't quite dishonesty. It's the Libra wish to keep the peace, using the Seven's cleverness to do it, and it holds right up until the two people compare notes.

At work it might be a compromise you've quietly engineered between two colleagues who'd never accept it if they knew it was yours. In a relationship it's smoothing things over so well that the real disagreement never gets aired. In a friendship it's the loyalty you're splitting between two friends who've fallen out. Choose one situation where you've been keeping everyone happy and say what you actually think.
sun.reversed:
Reversed, the Seven on a Libra Sun is often the peacekeeping arrangement coming undone. Two people you've been managing separately finally talk to each other. The compromise you arranged behind the scenes is traced back to you. Or you've avoided a decision for so long, keeping every option charming and open, that someone else made it for you. Air on air, overdone, can leave a Libra Sun with a lot of pleasant conversations and nothing settled.

At work that looks like being liked by everyone and trusted by fewer people than you'd hope. In love it can mean a partner who's worked out that you tell them what they want to hear. Make one decision this card has been circling, and tell everyone involved the same thing, in the same words.

moon.upright:
The Seven of Swords shows someone making off alone with an armful of blades, and a Libra Moon doesn't like doing anything alone. You feel steady when things are fair and pleasant between you and the people around you, and an atmosphere in the house can put you off your dinner. The card's Moon is a visitor in your Moon sign and takes Venus's colour here, and Aquarius trines Libra, air with air. So there's no clash of element. What there is, is a lot of thinking about feelings, and a habit of keeping the awkward ones out of sight so the room stays nice.

You'll know this one from the inside. Someone's upset you and you've decided it isn't worth the fuss. You're polite, even warm, and underneath you've quietly moved them down a rung. The Moon also rules Libra's first decan, the Two of Swords, a card about refusing to look at a choice, and a Libra Moon knows that stance well. With the Seven added, the feeling you haven't spoken starts making plans of its own.

With a partner, this is the calm you're keeping for their sake that's starting to cost you sleep. With a friend it's quietly seeing less of them and never saying why. At work it can mean agreeing in the meeting and feeling resentful on the train home. Try saying one small true thing that isn't nice. 'That annoyed me' is enough, with no apology after it.
moon.reversed:
With this card reversed, a Libra Moon can get very good at pretending there's no problem. The unfairness is real, a friend who always cancels, a partner who leaves you the boring jobs, and you keep smoothing it over until you can't remember what you felt in the first place. Venus colours the Moon here, so you'd prefer being liked to being right, and the Aquarian coolness lets you look perfectly serene while you do it.

It shows in relationships as a sweetness that's gone slightly brittle. In the body it tends to be a tiredness you can't quite account for. You don't have to start a war. Pick the one unfair thing you've been swallowing and raise it calmly, with the person it concerns, once.

rising.upright:
Venus rules your Ascendant, and Libra rising meets the world with good manners and a lot of charm. People find you easy company. With the Seven of Swords as your mask card, that charm has a purpose behind it. You're pleasant to everyone and you're also working something out, who has influence here, who you want on side, what you'd need to say to get the result you're after. Aquarius trines Libra, so the strategy and the grace sit together without friction.

That's also the risk. The same element amplifies, and air on air means a lot of words and very little resistance. You can talk your way into almost any room like this, and you'll feel how smoothly it's going. The trouble comes later, when someone realises your agreeable manner was carrying an agenda. The Moon is a visitor here, coloured by Venus, so the motive is rarely unkind. Usually you want peace, or approval, or one particular person to like you. It still counts as a plan, and people can tell when they've been handled nicely.

In a job interview it's saying the right thing so fluently that nobody learns anything real about you. With a new group of friends it's being liked by everyone within a week and close to nobody. In dating, it's the first few dates where you're charming and a bit strategic about how much to show. Go into your next new situation and disagree, politely, with one thing somebody says.
rising.reversed:
Libra rising with this card reversed can end up looking two-faced when you were only trying to be nice. You agreed with one person at lunch and the opposite person at dinner, and word travelled. Or your charm has become so polished that people wonder what's behind it. The Aquarian distance behind a Venus-ruled face makes you read as friendly and hard to reach.

It shows at work in the colleague who's decided you're political. With friends it's being invited everywhere and confided in by nobody. In a new relationship it can be the moment they notice you've never once said no to anything. The fix for Libra rising is small and uncomfortable. The next time you're asked what you think, answer before you've checked what everyone else thinks.

sun.upright:
Scorpio Suns already know how to keep a secret, so the Seven of Swords doesn't surprise you. It does sit awkwardly. The Moon is in fall in Scorpio, the sign where it's least comfortable, where it goes unheard and has to find an indirect way to do its job. And Aquarius squares Scorpio, two fixed signs three apart, a friction that forces action. So the card lands on your Sun with some grit in it. You're drawn to the private plan, and you're also more rattled than you'd like to admit by how much you've had to hide to make it work.

Scorpio wants depth, loyalty, everything or nothing. Aquarius, the card's sign, keeps a cool distance and changes allegiances on principle. Air and water haven't much to say to each other either. You'll feel it as being tempted to act strategically and disliking what that says about you. Or it goes the other way, and you notice someone else being strategic with you and your jaw sets. With a fixed square neither side backs down quickly, so this can run for a while.

At work it's the power struggle you're winning quietly, and the colleague who's starting to suspect. With money it might be an account, a debt or an arrangement you've kept from a partner. In a friendship it's knowing something you shouldn't and not having decided what to do with it. Ask yourself whether the secret you're keeping would still feel necessary if the other person already knew. Then act on the answer.
sun.reversed:
This reversed on a Scorpio Sun often means the secret has started to own you. You've kept something back so long, a plan, a feeling for someone, a grudge, a piece of information, that protecting it shapes your days. The Moon in fall can't say what it needs directly, and upside down it stops trying. You go quieter and more watchful, and the people close to you feel it without knowing what it is.

At work it's the strategy that's turned into an obsession. At home it's a partner asking what's wrong and getting 'nothing' for the fifth time. Scorpio is brave about the truth when it decides to be. Choose the person who'd be most affected by what you're holding and tell them yourself, before events decide for you.

moon.upright:
The Moon is in fall in Scorpio, so a Scorpio Moon has always felt things intensely and shown them sideways. You don't cry in public. You go quiet, you watch, you remember. A Moon card on your Moon makes that the whole story for a bit. The Seven of Swords has you protecting a feeling by hiding it, which you've done since you were small, and the card's sign, Aquarius, is square to Scorpio, both fixed, so the hiding tends to dig in.

What makes it hard is that Aquarius handles feelings by stepping back from them, and Scorpio handles them by going all the way in. Air and water have to be introduced to each other, and they haven't been. So you get a strange mix, a cool face over something very hot. You'll recognise lying awake working out what someone really meant, checking their messages for tone, and saying none of it. It's a way of staying safe. It also means you're carrying the whole thing on your own.

With a partner it's testing them without telling them there's a test. With family it can be the old hurt that nobody knows you still hold. Physically, this pairing tends to show as tension you hold for days and restless sleep. Trust is the currency for a Scorpio Moon, so spend a little. Tell one person something true about how you've been feeling, something you'd normally only admit to yourself.
moon.reversed:
When the Seven lands reversed on a Scorpio Moon, the private plan can turn into a private campaign. Someone hurt you, and instead of saying so you've started quietly arranging things, who you tell, who you freeze out, what you let slip. The Moon in fall already struggles to ask for what it needs, and reversed it stops asking and starts managing.

At home it looks like a long silence with a strategy inside it. With friends it's the group that's slowly split without anyone saying why. The body pays in poor sleep and a clenched stomach. Put the campaign down. Go to the person it's about and say what they did and how much it hurt, then listen to their side all the way through.

rising.upright:
People meet Scorpio rising and sense depth before you've said a word, a steady look, a feeling that you're reading them. Mars rules your Ascendant in the old system and Pluto in the modern one, and with the Seven of Swords as your mask card that reserve takes on a plan. You've come into this situation knowing more than you're showing, and you're fine with that.

The square between Aquarius and Scorpio gives it some edge. Both are fixed signs, and neither likes being told what to do. The card's Moon is in fall in your rising sign, so the feeling behind your face doesn't come through cleanly. It finds a side door. Strangers may read you as mysterious, which you don't mind, or as calculating, which you mind a lot. You'll notice yourself deciding very early who's safe and who isn't, and acting on it without explaining.

At work this is a real advantage in anything involving negotiation or investigation, where a poker face is worth money. In a new relationship it means keeping the most important thing about you back until you're sure. With neighbours or a new team it's the rumour you heard in the first week and have kept completely to yourself. Choose one person in a new situation and let them see your hand a little early, then watch what they do with it.
rising.reversed:
Scorpio rising with this card reversed can look much more secretive than you mean to. You've gone so guarded that people fill in the gaps themselves, and they don't fill them kindly. Or the plan you were quietly running gets spotted and you go very still, which only makes it look worse. The Moon's fall in this sign makes it hard to explain yourself on the spot.

At work it's a reputation for playing politics you never meant to earn. In love it's a new partner who feels shut out by the fourth date. Among friends it can be a misunderstanding you've let run because correcting it felt like exposing too much. Explain yourself once, without being asked, to whoever's got the wrong end of the stick.

sun.upright:
Sagittarius is the sign that says the awkward thing at dinner because it's true, so a card about keeping your reasons to yourself isn't your natural habitat. Still, the fit is friendlier than you'd guess. Aquarius is sextile Sagittarius, two signs apart, an easy opening you still have to take on purpose, and air feeds fire, so the card's cool thinking gives your enthusiasm something to run on. The Moon also rules the middle ten degrees of Sagittarius through the Nine of Wands, the card of the wary, worn-out figure still guarding the line, so this card's planet already knows your sign from the inside.

What you'll feel is a kind of restlessness with the group you're in. The Moon is a guest in your sign and takes Jupiter's colour, so its private motive is big and hopeful, a plan to get out, go further, try the thing nobody around you would try. The Seven says do it quietly. That's the hard part for a Sagittarius Sun. You'd much prefer to announce the trip, the course, the new venture, and hear everyone's opinion. Some of those opinions would talk you out of it, which is probably why the card is advising a bit of discretion.

At work it might be the application for the job overseas or the retraining you're weighing up. In a friendship group it's quietly outgrowing a scene you used to love. With a belief or a faith, it's doubts you haven't voiced yet. Get the plan to the point where it can survive a sceptical question, and then tell people.
sun.reversed:
For a Sagittarius Sun, the reversed card usually means the escape went wrong in some small way. You slipped out of a commitment with a breezy excuse and it's come back to bite. Or you've told yourself a big, optimistic story about why a shortcut was fine, and the Jupiter-coloured Moon, which likes to believe the best, went along with it. Sagittarius can talk itself into almost anything with enough conviction.

At work it's the corner cut on a deadline because you were already onto the next thing. With friends it's the promise made with total sincerity on a Friday night and forgotten by Monday. Go back to the one thing you left half-done when you got bored or restless, and either finish it or tell the people waiting on it that you won't.

moon.upright:
A Sagittarius Moon feels better with the horizon open. You need room, a trip booked, a plan for later, the knowledge that you could leave if you wanted to, even when you don't. The Seven of Swords feeds that. Air and fire are friendly, Aquarius is sextile to your Moon sign, and the card's figure is tiptoeing out of camp, which you'll understand in your bones. The Moon, only visiting here and coloured by Jupiter, makes the urge generous and optimistic, though it keeps its reasons to itself.

From the inside it feels like being fond of everyone and wanting to be somewhere else. You might be staying in a relationship, a job or a share house while quietly packing in your head, and feeling guilty about how cheerful that makes you. There's a small streak of evasion in it too. A Sagittarius Moon under this card will change the subject to something big and interesting whenever the conversation gets close to what it actually feels. And with the Moon also ruling the Nine of Wands decan of your sign, there's a tiredness under the restlessness that you probably haven't admitted.

With a partner, it shows as affection plus a very full calendar. With family it's the visit you keep putting off with enthusiasm about other plans. Your body tells you through sleep, the late nights, the second wind that isn't quite rest. Take the short trip, alone if you can, and use it to work out what you're actually leaving and what you're only tired of.
moon.reversed:
Turned upside down for a Sagittarius Moon, the card can mean running from a feeling by keeping busy. Another plan, another trip, another enthusiasm, anything to avoid sitting still with the thing that's upsetting you. The Jupiter-coloured Moon inflates, so even the running away gets presented to everyone as a great adventure. Friends can end up hearing about everything except what's wrong, and you'll have a funny story ready for when they ask.

It shows at home as restlessness that looks like fun and isn't. In relationships it can be a disappearing act done with a big smile. Sleep gets shorter. Cancel one plan you made mainly to get away from something, and use the free evening to feel whatever it was you were outrunning, even if it's dull or sad.

rising.upright:
Sagittarius rising comes through the door talking, friendly and frank and slightly too loud, the sort of person strangers tell their life story to in a queue. Jupiter rules your Ascendant, and it's Jupiter that colours the card's Moon in this sign, so the Seven of Swords sits on your manner as a bit of cheek. You're open about almost everything, and there's one thing you're keeping for later.

Air feeds fire, and the sextile between Aquarius and Sagittarius makes the strategy come easily if you choose to use it. The tension is more about your reputation. People expect Sagittarius rising to be completely straightforward, and when they catch a glimpse of a private agenda they can feel oddly let down, even if it's harmless. You'll also notice that you're charming your way through things you'd usually argue about, which is new for you, and probably effective.

In a sales job or a pitch, it's the big warm manner with a very clear target underneath. Travelling, it's talking your way into a better seat or out of a fee. In a new workplace it's being everyone's friend in the first fortnight while you quietly work out whether you're staying. When someone asks you a direct question, notice the urge to answer with a joke, and answer it straight at least once.
rising.reversed:
The reversed Seven for Sagittarius rising often shows up as being caught exaggerating. The story got bigger in the telling, the CV got a little generous, the promise came out full of confidence with no plan behind it. Jupiter's colour makes the Moon expansive, and when the card turns over the expansiveness starts to look like spin. Sagittarius rising usually gets forgiven a lot, though it can't count on it every time.

It tends to happen with new colleagues, new partners, new groups, anyone who hasn't known you long enough to know you mean well. They take the gap between what you said and what happened quite seriously. Say less than you're tempted to, promise only what you can see yourself doing, and when a story's been stretched, admit it cheerfully and give them the real version.

sun.upright:
Capricorn Suns build things to last, by the rules, with the receipts kept. This card is about the quiet workaround, and the astrology says the two have more in common than you'd think, which is partly a problem. Aquarius and Capricorn are neighbours, both ruled by Saturn in the old scheme, so the card's Moon takes its colour from your own ruler. But the Moon is in detriment in Capricorn, opposite its home in Cancer, and it has to work against the grain here. Feelings go underground. Plans are made quietly and carried out without comment.

That's the Capricorn Sun's version of this card. It isn't sly so much as private. You've worked out the smart route to the next rung, and you haven't discussed it with anyone because you don't discuss things until they're done. Air and earth are opposed, the idea against the proof, and you'll only believe the clever plan once it's working. The strain is that the Moon's needs, rest, comfort, being looked after, get pushed aside while the plan runs. I see this a lot with Capricorn Suns. The strategy is excellent and the person running it is exhausted.

At work it's positioning yourself for a role before anyone knows you want it. With money it's a savings plan or an investment you manage on your own. With a parent, often whoever set the standard in your house, it's proving something without saying so. Tell one person what you're aiming for, and let them help with a part of it.
sun.reversed:
For a Capricorn Sun the reversed card often shows up as a rule quietly bent to get a result. Usually nothing dramatic. A figure rounded up, a rival's idea taken further without credit, a policy used in a way it wasn't meant for. Capricorn respects structure so much that bending it feels like a private disgrace, so you justify it hard and never mention it. The Moon in detriment holds that kind of discomfort in the body, in the knees, the back, the teeth ground at night.

It also appears as coldness at home while you protect a work plan. Your partner gets the leftover hour. Go back over the last big result you're proud of and check whether anyone's owed a thank-you or some credit. Give it to them, in writing if you can.

moon.upright:
The Moon is in detriment in Capricorn, which is a technical way of saying a Capricorn Moon was never allowed much fuss. You learnt to manage, early. Feelings get handled like a job, dealt with efficiently and then filed. The Seven of Swords arrives from Aquarius, the sign next door, which shares Saturn as its old ruler, so the card's cool, private mood is one you already know well. You're good at keeping your needs to yourself. This card suggests you're doing more of it than usual.

From the inside it feels sensible. Someone asks how you are and you say busy, which is true. You're carrying a worry, about money, about a parent getting older, about your own energy, and you've made a plan for it and told nobody, because telling people would mean them fussing and you'd have to manage that as well. Air and earth pull against each other here, the plan in your head against the tired body that's carrying it. The two neighbouring signs each have what the other lacks, and what Aquarius has, a bit of distance and a sense of humour about it all, can help if you let it.

With a partner, this looks like being dependable and emotionally hard to find. With your own parents it's quietly organising things for them while never saying you're scared. Your sleep and your shoulders keep the real score. Hand one small worry to someone else, the insurance call, the booking, the conversation with your sibling, and let them do it their way.
moon.reversed:
Self-reliance hardening into secrecy is the usual shape of this card reversed for a Capricorn Moon. You're coping with something serious and nobody knows. Or you're so determined not to need anyone that you've started hiding small struggles from people who'd happily help, a bill, a bad week, a niggle in your health you're ignoring. The Moon in detriment already finds it hard to ask. Reversed, it stops even noticing it's allowed to.

The cost turns up in your body as stiffness and fatigue, and at home as a flatness your family can feel. At work you may be quietly doing the job of two. Pick one person and tell them one true thing about how hard it's been. You don't need to ask for anything yet. Just let them know.

rising.upright:
Capricorn rising meets the world looking capable, a bit formal, older than your years when you were young. Saturn rules your Ascendant, and Saturn is also the traditional ruler of Aquarius, the card's sign, so the Seven of Swords has a familiar landlord behind it. You arrive in new situations with a plan and a straight face, and people assume you know what you're doing, which you usually do.

The trouble is the Moon. It's in detriment in Capricorn, so the card's instinctive, feeling side doesn't show on your face at all. Add the card's secrecy to that and strangers can find you completely unreadable. The semi-sextile between the two signs means they're neighbours who don't naturally talk. Aquarius is detached and a bit odd, Capricorn is proper and ambitious, and the version of you people meet under this card is ambitious in a quiet, sideways way they may not spot until it's working.

At a new job it's learning how the place really runs before you make a move. In a negotiation it's giving nothing away until the other side has shown its hand. Meeting a partner's family, it's being polite, correct and completely closed. You'll get the results. What you might not get is warmth, so let one person see you when you're nervous, or pleased, or tired, and don't tidy it up for them.
rising.reversed:
Capricorn rising with the Seven upside down can come across as cold and calculating, which is harsh, and a little bit fair. You're pursuing something at work or in your social life with total focus, and people have noticed the focus but not the reason. The Moon in detriment makes the feeling behind the effort hard to see. Or the opposite happens and you've been caught taking a shortcut that doesn't fit your image as the proper one.

At a new job it can mean colleagues deciding you're after someone's position. It hurts your standing more than you'd expect, because Capricorn rising trades on being trustworthy. Explain your reasoning to the people it affects, before they guess, and own the shortcut if there was one. They'll mostly forgive the ambition once they understand it.

sun.upright:
This card is one of your sign's own. The Seven of Swords is the last ten degrees of Aquarius, ruled by the Moon, so an Aquarius Sun born late in the sign has it as a decan card, and every Aquarius Sun will recognise the figure, a person walking away from the crowd on their own logic with a slightly amused look. Air on air, card and sign, means the message comes through loud and clear. You're thinking your own way through something and you don't much want a committee.

The Moon has no special standing in Aquarius, neither helped nor held back, and it's coloured by Saturn in the old system and Uranus in the modern one. So the private motive here is either very principled or very contrary, and sometimes it's hard to tell which from the inside. You'll know the feeling of being sure you're right and not quite trusting the group enough to explain why. Aquarius is loyal to ideas and to people in general, and a bit harder to pin down with particular people. The card turns that up.

At work it's the independent project or the unpopular stance you're building a case for. In a friendship group it's drifting away to your own thing and being slightly surprised when people mind. In a community or a cause, it could be disagreeing with the line everyone's taking. Before you walk off with your idea, write down who it affects, and tell at least one of them what you're doing.
sun.reversed:
When the Seven turns over for an Aquarius Sun, independence can slide into contrariness. You're opposing something mainly because everyone else agrees with it. Or you've gone so far into your own clever plan that you've stopped checking it with anyone, and it has a flaw everybody else can see. Being native to your sign, the card doubles your blind spots as easily as your gifts. Aquarius hates being told it's being stubborn, which is usually a sign that it is.

At work it looks like the rebel who's quietly isolated. With friends it can mean going missing into a project and reappearing expecting nothing to have changed. With a partner it's explaining your feelings instead of having them. Take the idea you're proudest of to the person most likely to disagree with it, and listen properly to what they say.

moon.upright:
An Aquarius Moon handles feelings by getting a bit of distance on them. You feel safe when you have room to think, friends rather than a crowd, and nobody demanding an emotional response on the spot. The Seven of Swords is the Moon in Aquarius itself, the card's own planet in the card's own sign, so drawn on your Moon it's almost a description. The card belongs to the final decan of your sign, and it speaks your language fluently.

That fluency is the thing to watch. Same element, same sign, and nothing in the chart pushing back. You'll recognise the evening when someone wanted to talk about how they felt and you ended up discussing the situation in general, calmly and quite cleverly, and they went to bed feeling unheard. You weren't avoiding them deliberately. You work through emotion by thinking, and the Seven adds a private streak, so some of what you feel never makes it out of your head. The Moon here takes on Saturn's old coolness and some of Uranus's jumpiness, which means you can go from detached to suddenly needing space in an afternoon.

In a relationship, the need for room you haven't explained lands on the other person as rejection. With friends it's being the one who gives advice and never seems to need any. The body tends to register it as nervous energy, a buzzing head at bedtime. Once, try saying how you feel before you've worked out why.
moon.reversed:
The cool distance can freeze over when this card is reversed on an Aquarius Moon. You've stepped so far back from a feeling that you're watching your own life like a documentary, interested and oddly untouched. Or the private streak becomes a secret you're keeping about how unhappy something has made you, a job, a relationship, a group you've outgrown. The card is native to your sign, so there's nothing here to soften it.

It shows up with a partner as a sudden announcement that you need space, when you've needed it for months. With friends it's vanishing and resurfacing. In the body it's restlessness and poor sleep. Tell someone close about the feeling before you've decided what to do about it, so they're part of it early.

rising.upright:
Aquarius rising already comes across as a little different, friendly and interested and hard to place, the person at the party talking to the one guest nobody else approached. This card is native to your sign, the Moon's decan in the last ten degrees of Aquarius, and your chart ruler is Saturn in the old system and Uranus in the modern one, the same ruler colouring the card's Moon. So this card, worn as a mask, fits you like your own coat. You meet new situations with your own agenda, a cool head, and a readiness to leave quietly if it isn't for you.

Same element, and nothing to slow it down. That's the difficulty. People find you pleasant and slightly remote, and with this card they may also sense that you've already sized them up and decided something. You probably have. The Moon brings instinct into it, so your first reads are quick and often right, but you don't share them, and the other person is left wondering where they stand.

At a new job it's being the one who questions the process in week two, politely and with a better idea already worked out. In a club or a committee it's quietly organising a better version of it on the side. In dating it's being interesting and hard to get close to. When you meet someone new, tell them one thing you actually thought about them, kindly, out loud.
rising.reversed:
Aquarius rising, reversed Seven, can read as aloof to the point of rude. You've been so busy watching and working things out that you forgot to look friendly. Or you've been caught in a small evasion, a vague answer, a plan you didn't mention, and people who already found you hard to read have decided you're hiding something. The Moon's instincts are working fine. You just aren't letting anyone see them.

At work it's colleagues assuming you think you're above the team. In a new friendship it's the texts you meant to answer. In love it's a first impression of coolness you didn't intend. Warm up the front a few degrees. Ask people about themselves and remember what they said, then bring it up the next time you see them.

sun.upright:
Pisces Suns tend to go with the current, and a card about slipping away quietly with something tucked under your arm is closer to your habits than you'd like to admit. Aquarius is the sign right before Pisces, a neighbour with little in common with you, and each has what the other lacks. Aquarius has detachment and a clear head. Pisces has compassion and a feel for what isn't said. The card's Moon is a guest in Pisces, coloured by Jupiter, or by Neptune if you use the modern rulers, which makes its private motive softer and harder to see, even for you.

Air and water have to be introduced to each other, and in you they haven't quite met. You'll feel the Seven as a pull toward avoiding a situation instead of facing it, because you can see everyone's side and facing it would hurt somebody. So you drift out of the conversation, you agree to things you don't intend to do, you let people think what they want to think. It's kindly meant. It also leaves you carrying a lot of unfinished business that nobody else knows about.

In your work, especially creative or caring work, it can mean doing it your own way without telling your manager, and doing it well. At home there's the thing you haven't told your partner because you didn't want to upset them. With money, it's the account or the debt you've stopped opening letters about. Pick one of those and deal with it in full daylight, with someone beside you if that helps.
sun.reversed:
Pisces Suns under the reversed Seven often end up telling small stories to keep the peace, and then believing them. You said you were fine, you said the job was going well, you said you'd already sent it. None of it quite true, none of it malicious. The Neptune-tinted Moon blurs the line between a hope and a fact, and the card upside down lets the blur spread.

At work that can look like a deadline that's been quietly slipping for weeks. In love it's a partner who can't get a straight answer and has stopped asking. Choose one of those stories and correct it, gently, with the person who heard it. It'll be awkward for a few minutes.

moon.upright:
A Pisces Moon soaks up whatever's in the room. You feel other people's moods before they've said anything, and you need regular time alone to wring yourself out. The Seven of Swords gives that need a secretive edge. The card's Moon has no special standing in Pisces and takes Jupiter's colour, or Neptune's, so it's generous and dreamy, and the card's Aquarian sign is the one just before yours, close by and quite unlike you.

The two signs share almost nothing, which turns out to be useful, because Aquarius can do the one thing Pisces struggles with. It can step back. With this card on your Moon you're learning to step back, and it doesn't feel natural, so it comes out sideways, as slipping away. You leave the party without saying goodbye. You let calls go to voicemail. You invent a reason you can't come, because the real reason, that you've absorbed too much and need to be alone, sounds too odd to say. Air and water have to be introduced, and here the introduction is you taking space without asking permission for it.

With a partner it's needing more solitude than you've admitted. With family it's quietly avoiding the relative who drains you. The body shows it in tiredness and in how much sleep you need. Tell the people who matter that you need time to yourself, in those words, and stop making up the excuses.
moon.reversed:
For a Pisces Moon, the card reversed can mean hiding from your own feelings in a softer way. Too much television, too many hours scrolling, too many late snacks, a comfortable fog that keeps whatever's underneath from surfacing. A Neptune-coloured Moon is good at fog. Upside down, the Seven's private streak turns inward, and you start keeping secrets from yourself about how you really are. It's gentle, which is why it can go on for so long.

People close to you can tell something's off but can't reach it. Sleep goes strange, too long or too broken. Start small. For a week, notice each time you reach for the fog, and on one of those evenings text a friend and tell them you've been struggling a bit.

rising.upright:
Pisces rising meets people softly. You come across as gentle, a bit hard to pin down, the sort of person strangers confide in without knowing why. Jupiter rules your Ascendant in the traditional scheme and Neptune in the modern one, and the card's Moon borrows that colour in Pisces, so the card shows in your manner as an elusiveness more than a scheme. You slip through situations. People aren't quite sure afterwards what you actually said.

Aquarius sits just behind Pisces in the zodiac, and the semi-sextile means the card and your rising sign are neighbours who've never really understood each other. Aquarius is cool and deliberate about keeping its distance. Pisces rising does it by being vague and agreeable. With the card added you're doing both, friendly on the surface and quietly keeping your own counsel. It's protective, and it often works. Strangers find you easy to be with and very hard to know.

In a new job it's being well liked and never quite clear about what you want. When you're dating, it's becoming whatever the other person seems to want, then vanishing when it gets too much. In a group it's slipping out early from every gathering so nobody notices you leaving. The next time someone asks what you'd like, where to eat, what to watch, which job you're after, give a specific answer.
rising.reversed:
Pisces rising with the card upside down can seem evasive in a way that frustrates people. You didn't answer the question, you said yes and meant maybe, you went quiet in the group chat for a week and came back as if nothing had happened. It isn't calculated. It's a way of getting out of the room without a scene, and the Moon, softened by Neptune, makes it feel perfectly natural.

At work it can mean a reputation for being lovely and unreliable. With a new partner it's the mixed signals they keep trying to decode. With friends it's the plans you agree to and then quietly drop. Say no clearly, once, to something you'd normally drift out of, and see how much simpler that makes the following week.

1.upright:
How you come across, your body, the way you carry yourself and the way you start things, all belong to the first house. With this card here, what's live is how much of yourself you're letting show. You're starting something on your own terms, a new look, a new role, a new approach to an old problem, and you're keeping the reasoning back. The house is angular, one of the chart's four corners, so whatever lands here doesn't stay quiet for long, even when the card would like it to.

Aries is the first house's natural sign, and Aquarius sits sextile to it, two signs along, a friendly angle that only pays off if you act on it. Air feeding fire helps too, and Mercury, which has its joy in this house, suits the card's cleverness. So the strategy and the urge to begin get on reasonably well. The strain comes from the Moon. The first house is about being seen, and this card's Moon prefers to work unseen, so you may notice yourself walking into rooms with a composed face and a lot going on behind it. People might describe you as hard to read. You'd probably take that as a compliment.

With your body, it can show up as ignoring what it's telling you because you've decided on a plan and don't want to be slowed down. With your appearance, it's a change you've made partly to be taken differently, a haircut, a new way of dressing for work. In how you start things, it's beginning quietly and only telling people once it's underway. Keep the plan private if you like, and be honest with yourself about why you are.
1.reversed:
Turned over in the first house, the card can mean a front that's got harder to hold. You've been presenting a version of yourself, more sorted, more certain, less bothered than you really are, and it's tiring. Or you've started something in secret and it's shown on your face before you were ready to explain it. The angular house doesn't let things stay hidden, and reversed, the Seven stops trying very hard to hide them.

It tends to show up in the body first, poor sleep, tension, looking tired to people who know you. It also shows in first impressions going oddly, people reading you as guarded when you meant to seem calm. Drop one piece of the act with somebody new, a nervousness, an uncertainty, and see whether they like you better for it.

2.upright:
The second house is your actual money and what you think you're worth, which are more closely tied than most people like to admit.
